Welcome! This is my personal, evolving set of notes taken while working through
Carnegie Mellon University's
[AI Engineering Fundamentals graduate certificate](https://www.cmu.edu/online/ai-engineering-fundamentals),
starting with course **24-887 — Machine Learning & AI for Engineers**, and
[Calculus I at the University of North Dakota](https://und.edu/academics/online/enroll-anytime/math165.html)
to strengthen the math foundation underneath.

These courses are part of my preparation for a **Master of Science in Computer
Science**. The full plan — four tracks covering computer science, applied AI, math
foundations, and applied math — is on the [Learning Path](learning-path.qmd) page.

I write these notes mostly to understand things more deeply (e.g. deriving the
gradient-descent update rules by hand, even though real projects would just use a
library) and to keep a searchable refresher for my future self.

## Machine learning

- [Logistic Regression](notes/logistic-regression/index.qmd) — binary, multi-class,
  and non-linear classification, starting from deriving gradient descent by hand.
- [Support Vector Machine](notes/support-vector-machine/index.qmd) — max-margin
  classification, deriving the weights form and the support-vector (dual) form by hand.
- [Neural Networks](notes/neural-networks/index.qmd) — forward propagation through a
  fully connected layer, activation functions, and softmax.

## Mathematics

- [Calculus I (UND Math 165)](notes/calculus-1/index.qmd) — key definitions,
  theorems, and rules for limits and derivatives, plus a one-page quick reference.

## Credit

- **Machine learning notes:** course material and problem framing are from CMU's
  **24-887 — Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence for Engineers** (instructor:
  Professor Levent Burak Kara), part of the
  [AI Engineering Fundamentals](https://www.cmu.edu/online/ai-engineering-fundamentals)
  graduate certificate.
- **Calculus notes:** definitions and theorems are reproduced from *APEX Calculus*
  (© 2015 Gregory Hartman, © 2025 Department of Mathematics, University of North
  Dakota) under [CC BY-NC 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/), for
  UND's Math 165: Calculus I.

These are my own study notes; any errors are mine.
